Best: E010, 6.639 s, 0.7548 (8.5 ep, Muon+EMA+prog-res 24/28/32, last width 512). The margin over the 0.753 bar is 0.17 pp.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete): E001 9ep eager 0.7430/9.43. E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 +prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 8.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564/6.99. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 is an exact rerun of E010: 0.754767 and 6.646 s, so accuracy is bit-identical and time repeats within 0.1%.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs about 0.18 pp and saves 4.8% time (E007 to E008). Roughly linear.
2. Compile: E003's slowness was a recompile leak. E004 fixed it with stride matching, and compile alone saved about 4%.
3. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s (E004 to E005). This is the cheapest gain measured and larger than any theory predicted.
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s (E005 to E006).
5. Progressive resizing: -22% time for -0.59 pp (E006 to E007). Time tracks pixel count.
6. Width 576 to 512: -4.8% time for -0.25 pp, about the same exchange rate as the epoch dial.
7. LR floor 0 on top of EMA: no gain (-0.08 pp, E009). EMA and the low final LR are redundant.
8. Resolution cliff (E011): -14% time for -1.4 pp, about 3x worse than the E007 rate. The 20 px phase is costly.
9. Noise: compiled runs are deterministic per seed (E012 matches E010 exactly), so the noise that matters is seed-to-seed and recipe-reshuffle, about ±0.2 pp on 3-seed means. Time noise is about 1% or less. Fixed costs are about 0.3-0.5 s.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and resizing, and over-predicted E009 and E011 accuracy. Measured wins have repeatedly exceeded my ranges, so I should widen the upside on accuracy-positive changes. But untested tweaks (lr, wd) have no measured trend to extrapolate, so I centre them near zero effect.

Unsure: GPU idle time and launch overhead under 4 CPUs (CUDA graphs could save 0-10%). Also unsure whether lr, wd and label smoothing are tuned for CIFAR-100, whether a plain EMA matches Lookahead, and the held-out seed spread. The margin is thin, so accuracy-neutral systems changes are the safest time wins. Any accuracy-positive tweak could be spent on epochs, at about 0.18 pp per 4.8% of time."}

forecasts.reason: Compiled steps with batch 2000 are already GPU-bound; cudagraphs may save a few percent, but the Muon plus multi-resolution capture is risky and the fixed overhead stays.
Muon lr is untuned for CIFAR-100; the direction is uncertain, and the expected gain is small relative to the 0.2 pp noise.
Halving wd could go either way. EMA plus a short run suggests a mild gain, but nothing measured supports it.
Dynamo graph breaks probably sit only in the Muon optimizer and the Python loop. Removing them gives a small gain at best.
Lookahead's reset of the fast weights likely contributes beyond a plain EMA. A plain EMA with a late-ramped alpha probably loses accuracy, and the margin is thin.

cruxes: Is the GPU idle or launch-bound under the 4-CPU pin? If it is idle more than 10%, CUDA graphs are a free win. If not, systems changes are nearly worthless.
Are Muon lr, wd and label smoothing near-optimal for CIFAR-100? Any accuracy-positive retune could be spent on epochs, at about 0.18 pp per 4.8% of time.
What is the held-out 40-seed mean for E010 (E012 diagnostic)? If it is below 0.75, the current best is invalid and the margin must be rebuilt.
